LBR.note: No public procurement system is mentioned.

facts.fact: Governor Saamoi says the Central Bank of Liberia launched the Inclusive Instant Payment System (Pay Na-Na), mobile money interoperability, as the first phase of the National Electronic Payment Switch, with a pilot completed earlier in 2025.

LBR.note: Cybersecurity is mentioned, with no consumer rule or complaints body.
Cross-border transactions are only listed as a future use case.

facts.fact: Governor Saamoi says the IIPS pilot phase offers person-to-person and government-to-people real-time transactions, and that salaries, pensions and social transfers will be delivered through it.
Governor Saamoi's speech names Lonestar Cell MTN Mobile Money Corporation and Orange Money Liberia as the mobile money operators taking part in the IIPS launch.
Governor Saamoi says the Central Bank of Liberia launched the IIPS as mobile money interoperability, with the pilot phase live for person-to-person transactions.
Governor Saamoi says people-to-government payment of taxes through the IIPS is ongoing with the Liberia Revenue Authority.
